title: Padres Add Joe Musgrove to Wild Card Roster After Nearly Two-Year Injury Absence
dek: The San Diego Padres added right-hander Joe Musgrove to their 26-player Wild Card roster against the Chicago Cubs. Musgrove has not pitched in an MLB game since October 2, 2024, after undergoing Tommy John surgery for a torn UCL; his recovery was marked by setbacks including a back injury that delayed his return.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Musgrove, 33, has not pitched in the majors for nearly two years after Tommy John surgery in October 2024 and is now active for the postseason, likely as a bullpen option despite uncertainty about his durability.
bottom_line: Musgrove's availability will depend on the Wild Card Series' length and game situation. Whether he can effectively transition from instructional work and minor-league rehab to postseason competition after two years away will become clear only if and when the Padres call on him; his fastball velocity recovery and recent statements suggest confidence, but the extended absence and back setback represent genuine risk.
body: The San Diego Padres added right-hander Joe Musgrove to their 26-player Wild Card roster against the Chicago Cubs, according to CBS Sports MLB reporting on September 29. Should Musgrove pitch in the 2026 postseason, it will be his first major-league game action in nearly two years.

Musgrove has not pitched in the majors since making a start against the Braves in Game 2 of the 2024 Wild Card Series on October 2, 2024. Shortly after that appearance, the 33-year-old was diagnosed with a torn UCL in his throwing elbow and underwent Tommy John surgery in October 2024. His recovery has been marked by setbacks: earlier this season, Musgrove made four minor-league rehab starts, but his return to the Padres was pushed back because of a back issue, per CBS Sports MLB.

Musgrove has shown positive signs in his recent preparation. In his three August rehab starts at Triple-A, he averaged 94.4 mph with his fastball, according to CBS Sports MLB, up from his 2024 season average of 92.9 mph. He also demonstrated good stuff in recent instructional league appearances and live batting practice, per the San Diego Union-Tribune as reported by CBS Sports MLB. In a statement on Sunday, Musgrove said: "I don't know if it's the shorter outings or if we've finally reached a point where my arm is just feeling healthy.... I do feel the most optimistic I've felt at any time in the last two years."

A role in the bullpen seems the most likely use for Musgrove, CBS Sports MLB reports. The Padres have the strongest and deepest bullpen in these playoffs, but uncertainty exists in the rotation after their first two starters. Michael King posted a 2.74 ERA at home in 2026, while Nick Pivetta is making just his fifth start since returning from a nearly five-month absence due to an elbow injury, having allowed three runs over 18 2/3 innings in his four outings since rejoining the rotation, per CBS Sports Betting reporting.

Over his four seasons with the Padres, Musgrove boasts an ERA+ of 123 with an FIP of 3.68 and a 4.18 K/BB ratio across 97 starts and one relief appearance, according to CBS Sports MLB. He threw the first no-hitter in Padres history in 2021. Across his MLB career, Musgrove has made 26 relief appearances and an additional four relief appearances in the postseason, per CBS Sports MLB, lending some experience to a bullpen role despite his extended absence from competition.
